acoustic-insulation.q: How much does acoustic insulation cost in Australia?
acoustic-insulation.a: Acoustic insulation costs $10 to $25 per square metre installed in Australia, with acoustic batts themselves running around $75 a pack at retail. Total price depends on wall or ceiling area, batt thickness, and whether plasterboard needs removing and refitting around the new batts. A single internal wall usually sits at the lower end.

acoustic-insulation.q: Does acoustic insulation actually reduce noise?
acoustic-insulation.a: Acoustic insulation does reduce noise, though it will not block sound entirely. Dense glasswool or polyester batts fitted snugly between wall or ceiling studs absorb airborne noise like voices, TVs, and traffic. Pairing batts with acoustic sealant around gaps and resilient mounts on plasterboard improves results further.

acoustic-insulation.q: Where is acoustic insulation most worth installing?
acoustic-insulation.a: Acoustic insulation gives the best return in shared walls between bedrooms, home theatres, laundries, and walls facing busy streets. Ceilings under upstairs living areas also benefit. Installers typically use higher-density batts in these spots than standard thermal insulation, since sound absorption depends more on density than R-value.

bathroom-tap-installation.q: How much does bathroom tap installation cost in Australia?
bathroom-tap-installation.a: Installing a bathroom tap costs $150 to $400 in Australia for a straightforward swap, covering the tap itself ($90 to $325) plus one to two hours of licensed plumber labour at $80 to $200 an hour. Costs rise if old pipework needs replacing or the vanity needs reconfiguring.

bathroom-tap-installation.q: Can I install a bathroom tap myself?
bathroom-tap-installation.a: You can fit a like-for-like tap yourself if you are comfortable with basic plumbing and turn off the water first, but any change to pipe layout or fitting a new mixer legally requires a licensed plumber in Australia. Getting the seal wrong risks leaks inside the vanity or wall.

bathroom-tap-installation.q: How long does a bathroom tap last before it needs replacing?
bathroom-tap-installation.a: A quality mixer tap typically lasts 10 to 15 years before washers, cartridges, or the finish wear out. Cheaper taps may need cartridge replacement within a few years. Signs it is time to replace rather than repair include persistent dripping, stiff handles, and corrosion around the base or spout.

cement-rendering.q: How much does cement rendering cost in Australia?
cement-rendering.a: Cement rendering costs $30 to $80 per square metre installed in Australia, including polymer render mix (around $15 per 20kg bag) and reinforcing mesh (about $51 a roll). A full house elevation adds up quickly, so most homeowners get a per-wall quote rather than costing it bag by bag.

cement-rendering.q: Can you render over old brickwork?
cement-rendering.a: Cement render can go over most brick, block, and besser walls provided the surface is clean, structurally sound, and free of loose paint or efflorescence. Cracked or crumbling brickwork needs repair first, and a bonding agent or mesh is often added to help the new render key in properly.

cement-rendering.q: Does cement render crack over time?
cement-rendering.a: Cement render can develop hairline cracks over time from building movement, poor mixing, or applying coats too thick or too fast. Reinforcing mesh in corners and control joints reduces the risk. Fine cracks are usually cosmetic and easy to patch, but wider cracks should be checked by a renderer.

deck-sanding-and-sealing.q: How much does deck sanding and sealing cost in Australia?
deck-sanding-and-sealing.a: Deck sanding and sealing typically costs $35 to $70 per square metre in Australia, including sanding, cleanup, and two coats of exterior decking oil (around $70 to $296 per 10 litre tin). A standard 20 to 30 square metre deck usually runs $700 to $2,100 depending on timber condition and access.

deck-sanding-and-sealing.q: How often should a timber deck be sanded and resealed?
deck-sanding-and-sealing.a: Most timber decks need resealing with oil or stain every one to two years to keep water resistance up, while a full sand back is usually only needed every five to ten years once the timber greys, splinters, or the old coating flakes badly. Sun exposure and foot traffic speed up wear.

deck-sanding-and-sealing.q: Can I sand and seal a deck myself?
deck-sanding-and-sealing.a: Sanding and sealing a deck yourself is a realistic DIY job with a hired drum or orbital sander, though it is physically demanding and dusty. Getting even coverage on oil and avoiding lap marks takes practice, so many homeowners hire a professional for decks over about 20 square metres.

fence-gate-installation.q: How much does it cost to install a fence gate in Australia?
fence-gate-installation.a: A single fence gate installation costs $150 to $400 in Australia, covering hinge and latch hardware ($17 to $85) plus timber framing and labour at standard fencing rates of $100 to $180 per metre. Wider double gates or steel driveway gates cost more due to extra bracing and hardware.

fence-gate-installation.q: What makes a gate sag over time?
fence-gate-installation.a: Gates sag mainly from undersized hinges, posts that were not set deep enough in concrete, or timber framing that lacks a diagonal brace. Heavier gates put more strain on the top hinge in particular. Fitting a diagonal turnbuckle brace and using galvanised hinges rated for the gate weight prevents most sagging.

fence-gate-installation.q: How long does it take to install a fence gate?
fence-gate-installation.a: A single fence gate installation usually takes half a day to a full day once posts are set, including trimming and fitting hardware. Concrete around new posts needs 24 to 48 hours to cure before the gate can safely take weight, so tradespeople often return the next day to hang it.

garden-path-paving.q: How much does garden path paving cost in Australia?
garden-path-paving.a: Garden path paving costs $50 to $150 per square metre installed in Australia, including concrete pavers (around $15 each for a 400x400mm size), bedding sand, and a compacted crusher dust base. A narrow one metre wide path across a typical backyard usually lands toward the lower end of that range.

garden-path-paving.q: What is the best base for a garden path?
garden-path-paving.a: A compacted crusher dust base over a layer of road base is the standard foundation for a garden path in Australia, giving pavers a stable, well drained surface that resists shifting. Skipping proper compaction is the most common cause of pavers sinking or going uneven within a year or two.

garden-path-paving.q: Can I lay a garden path myself?
garden-path-paving.a: Laying a simple garden path is a realistic DIY project for a straight, narrow path over firm ground, using pavers, sand, and a hand tamper. Curved paths, sloped sites, or areas near tree roots are harder to get level and drained properly, so those jobs are usually better left to a paver.

house-slab-pouring.q: How much does it cost to pour a house slab in Australia?
house-slab-pouring.a: Pouring a house slab costs $50 to $150 per square metre in Australia, including reinforcing mesh, formwork, and concrete. A standard 100 to 150 square metre home slab typically totals $5,000 to $22,500 depending on soil conditions, site access, and whether extra excavation or engineering is required.

house-slab-pouring.q: How thick does a house slab need to be?
house-slab-pouring.a: A standard residential house slab is usually poured around 100mm thick for the main area, with thickened edge beams and footings sized by an engineer based on soil classification. Reactive clay soils often need a thicker, more heavily reinforced slab than sand or rock, which is why engineering reports vary in cost.

house-slab-pouring.q: How long does a house slab need to cure before building?
house-slab-pouring.a: A house slab reaches enough strength to build on after about seven days, though full concrete strength takes around 28 days to develop. Builders typically wait at least a week before starting frame work, and formwork is usually stripped after two to three days once the edges have set.

leaf-guard-installation.q: How much does leaf guard installation cost in Australia?
leaf-guard-installation.a: Leaf guard installation costs $30 to $80 per metre in Australia, including gutter mesh (around $285 a roll) and fitting along the existing gutter line. A typical single storey home with 30 to 40 metres of guttering usually costs $900 to $3,200 depending on roof pitch and access.

leaf-guard-installation.q: Does leaf guard stop gutters blocking completely?
leaf-guard-installation.a: Leaf guard mesh significantly reduces blockages by keeping out leaves and larger debris, but it does not stop everything. Fine debris like gum leaves, pine needles, or seed pods can still build up on top of the mesh over time, so gutters still need an occasional clean, just far less often.

leaf-guard-installation.q: Can I install gutter leaf guard myself?
leaf-guard-installation.a: Installing gutter leaf guard yourself is possible for a single storey home with safe roof access, using clip-in or screw-fix mesh sold at hardware stores. Two storey homes or steep roofs are safer left to a professional, since most leaf guard injuries come from ladder falls rather than the job itself.

plasterboard-installation.q: Is plasterboard the same as Gyprock?
plasterboard-installation.a: Plasterboard is the generic term for gypsum board, while Gyprock is a specific brand of plasterboard made by CSR, similar to how Kleenex is a brand of tissue. Tradespeople in Australia often say Gyprock out of habit even when installing a different brand like Boral or USG, since the products are functionally the same.

9mm plasterboard suits ceilings on closely spaced trusses and standard wall linings in most homes, while 12mm plasterboard is the sturdier choice for walls needing extra strength or wider stud spacing. Wet areas and garage walls often use the thicker 12mm sheet for better impact resistance and fire performance.

plasterboard-installation.q: How much does plasterboard installation cost in Australia?
plasterboard-installation.a: Plasterboard installation costs $45 to $90 per hour for a plasterer in Australia, with sheets themselves running $28 to $97 each depending on size and thickness. A standard room typically needs several sheets plus base coat, jointing tape, and topping compound, adding roughly $80 to $150 in material costs on top of labour.

ridge-capping-repair.q: How much does ridge capping repair cost in Australia?
ridge-capping-repair.a: Ridge capping repair costs $50 to $100 an hour for a roofer in Australia, with most jobs taking two to four hours depending on how many ridge lengths need repointing or replacing. Materials add roughly $40 for flexible roof pointing plus around $50 per metre of new Colorbond capping if sections are damaged.

ridge-capping-repair.q: What causes ridge capping to fail?
ridge-capping-repair.a: Ridge capping usually fails when the old cement pointing that seals it to the tiles or sheets dries out, shrinks, and cracks over 15 to 20 years, letting water in underneath. Storm damage, tile movement, and corrosion on metal roofs can also loosen ridge capping earlier than that.

ridge-capping-repair.q: How do I know if my ridge capping needs repair?
ridge-capping-repair.a: Signs your ridge capping needs repair include visible cracks or gaps in the pointing along the roof ridge, ceiling stains after rain, capping that looks lifted or loose, and crumbling cement visible from the ground. A roofer can confirm the extent of the damage during an on-roof inspection before quoting.

skylight-installation.q: How much does skylight installation cost in Australia?
skylight-installation.a: Skylight installation costs $900 to $3,500 in Australia including the skylight unit and roofer's labour, depending on the type. Tubular skylights run from about $770 to $2,700 for the unit alone, plus flashing (around $65) and typically half a day of roofing labour at $50 to $100 an hour.

skylight-installation.q: What are the downsides of skylights?
skylight-installation.a: The main downsides of skylights are heat gain in summer, potential heat loss in winter without double glazing, and the risk of leaks if flashing is fitted poorly or ages without maintenance. Tubular skylights avoid most of these issues since they use a small roof-level dome rather than a large glass panel.

A well installed skylight with correctly fitted flashing should not leak, and most leaks trace back to deteriorated flashing seals, cracked sealant, or debris build up around the unit rather than the skylight itself. Getting flashing checked every few years, especially after storms, prevents most water ingress problems before they start.

tile-regrouting.q: How much does tile regrouting cost in Australia?
tile-regrouting.a: Tile regrouting costs $15 to $40 per square metre in Australia for labour, since the job is mostly removing old grout and repacking new grout rather than buying tiles. A standard bathroom typically costs $300 to $700 total, with grout itself only adding about $12 to $33 per 5kg bag.

tile-regrouting.q: How often should tile grout be redone?
tile-regrouting.a: Tile grout typically needs redoing every 10 to 15 years in normal areas, but wet areas like showers can need it sooner, often every 5 to 8 years, once grout turns porous, stains, or starts crumbling. Regrouting before grout fails completely helps prevent water getting behind tiles and causing hidden damage.

Regrouting tiles yourself is achievable for a small area with a grout removal tool, new grout, and a rubber float, and many homeowners tackle a splashback or small bathroom this way. Showers and large wet areas are trickier because poor grout removal or sealing can let water through, so mistakes cost more to fix.

wall-tiling.q: How much does wall tiling cost in Australia?
wall-tiling.a: Wall tiling costs $45 to $120 per square metre installed in Australia, including ceramic tiles (around $14 to $59 per square metre), adhesive, and grout. A standard bathroom or kitchen splashback wall typically costs $500 to $1,500 total depending on tile size, pattern complexity, and how much surface prep is needed first.

wall-tiling.q: Do I need to waterproof a wall before tiling?
wall-tiling.a: Wet areas like showers need a waterproofing membrane applied before tiling, while splashbacks and other dry walls generally do not. Skipping waterproofing in a shower risks water tracking through grout lines into the wall cavity, leading to mould and hidden damage that costs far more to fix later than the membrane itself would have.

wall-tiling.q: What size tiles make a small bathroom wall look bigger?
wall-tiling.a: Larger format tiles, generally 300x600mm or bigger, make a small bathroom wall look bigger by reducing the number of grout lines breaking up the surface. Lighter colours and a single tile run floor to ceiling add to the effect. Small mosaic tiles tend to visually shrink a space despite being popular for feature strips.
